overview: Al-Adil I was Saladin’s brother, a diplomat and ruler who preserved Ayyubid power after Saladin and dealt with crusader states and the Fifth Crusade.
He is remembered as a stabilizer of the Ayyubid world, less famous than Saladin but vital to the dynasty’s survival.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Al-Adil I was Saladin’s brother, a diplomat and ruler who preserved Ayyubid power after Saladin and dealt with crusader states and the Fifth Crusade.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Al-Adil grew up within the same Kurdish military family as Saladin and served in campaigns that created the Ayyubid Sultanate.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Al-Adil I, brother of Saladin, is remembered as a shrewd, patient, and supremely capable administrator and diplomat, the steady hand who held the Ayyubid realm together. Both Muslim and crusader sources — to the latter he was known as Saphadin — present a ruler whose talents lay less in battlefield glory than in governance, negotiation, and the careful management of a sprawling family confederation.

He served as Saladin's indispensable lieutenant and then, after a period of skilful maneuvering among his nephews, secured supreme power for himself, governing with a pragmatism that favoured truces and trade with the crusader states over endless war. The sources credit him with political subtlety and financial acumen rather than the charisma or piety emphasised in his brother's legend.

What the record conveys is a calculating and effective statesman who valued stability and consolidation — the organiser who turned Saladin's conquests into a durable dynastic structure. He is remembered as the patient diplomat-administrator of the Ayyubid house, whose quiet competence preserved and ordered what his more famous brother had won.

contentSections.title: As Ayyubid sultan
paragraphs: Al-Adil balanced Ayyubid family politics, negotiated with Latin rulers, and eventually ruled Egypt and Syria. His diplomacy with Richard the Lionheart and later pressure during the Fifth Crusade show his long career.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Al-Adil died in 1218 during the crisis caused by the Fifth Crusade’s attack on Damietta, leaving Ayyubid leadership to his sons.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: He is remembered as a stabilizer of the Ayyubid world, less famous than Saladin but vital to the dynasty’s survival.
